quizzes.stem: Scenario: Linden Clinics asks a vendor to serve its patients from Europe and offers the Claude API with `inference_geo` set to `us` as the compliant option. Which assessment is right?

options.a: It meets the need, as long as the audit log itself is kept in a data store located in Europe
options.b: It fails the need, because that pin places all of the processing in the United States
options.c: It meets the need, since the geography of the workspace can still be set to Europe separately
options.d: It fails the need only if the clinics have not yet signed the business associate agreement in full

explanation.b: The `us` pin is a United States geography, and the API has no European one.
explanation.a: Ruled out because where the log is stored does not move inference, and "A customer that needs Europe cannot be served by pinning on that API".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The workspace geography is set per workspace" and the page says it is `us` only.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the agreement concerns health data and does not move the processing: "there is no European pin".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Harrow Insurance runs Claude on Amazon Bedrock and writes in its design that "zero data retention is enabled with Anthropic". What is the problem?

options.a: The statement is correct, since every platform shares one retention arrangement with the model maker
options.b: The statement holds, provided the company has also signed a business associate agreement with Anthropic
options.c: The statement is wrong, since the arrangement is the model maker's and the cloud provider is the processor
options.d: The statement is correct, but it must be repeated for each separate model that the company uses in production

explanation.c: Zero data retention is an arrangement with Anthropic, and on Bedrock the cloud provider is the processor.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Their retention, compliance and region rules are the provider's", so no arrangement is shared.
explanation.b: Ruled out because that agreement is a separate arrangement, and "On Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud, zero data retention is not Anthropic's arrangement to give".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model is a separate rule ("A model that requires 30-day retention cannot satisfy a zero-retention requirement") and does not change who the processor is.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Fennel Health's drafting assistant receives claim notes with patient names, contact details and policy numbers. Which design best keeps these away from the model provider?

options.a: A system prompt that instructs the model to ignore any personal details it comes across
options.b: A review step that checks the model's reply for personal details after it has been returned
options.c: A larger model that is better at noticing which parts of a note are sensitive ones
options.d: A step in the caller that swaps each identifier for a token and puts the values back afterwards

explanation.d: A layer before the call means the provider sees tokens and never the values, and the layer can be tested.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the data has already crossed the boundary".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a larger model still receives the data, and "a compliance control belongs in the architecture where it can be tested".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a check on the reply, like an instruction, "acts after the data has already crossed the boundary".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Rook Mutual's auditors ask for proof of each model call. The team proposes logging every full prompt and reply for ten years. What should the architect say?

options.a: Log each call's id, caller, time and size, and pull content from the source records only when needed
options.b: Accept the proposal, since a complete record is the strongest evidence that a regulator can ask to see
options.c: Log full content, but encrypt the log, which removes the obligations that a data store has
options.d: Log nothing from the calls, since any stored record of a call becomes a risk in itself

explanation.a: The log proves what happened without becoming a second copy of the data.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the log becomes a second store of sensitive data with its own obligations".
explanation.c: Ruled out because encryption protects a store and does not remove it: the log would still be "a store of health or personal data, with all the obligations of one".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an audit log must record "who, when, which request and what size".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Marlow Care's service holds data of patients in the United States and in the European Union. It runs a deployment in each region. A European patient's request arrives while the European deployment is down for maintenance. What should the router do?

options.a: Turn it away for now with an error, and let the caller try again once the local site is back up
options.b: Send it to the United States deployment, since being available matters more than where the data sits
options.c: Send it to the United States deployment, after tokenising the identifiers in the request
options.d: Send it to whichever deployment answers the fastest, and record the exception in the audit log

explanation.a: Serving the user from another region breaks the residency requirement, so with no deployment that keeps the data in the region the answer is none.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "serving a European user from a United States deployment because it was available is the failure the router exists to prevent".
explanation.c: Ruled out because tokenising does not change where the request is processed, and "a user's data goes only to a deployment that keeps it in the user's region".
explanation.d: Ruled out because speed is not a criterion, and the router sends a user's data "only to a deployment that keeps it in that region".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Alder Dental needs zero data retention on its Claude API deployment and has chosen a model that requires 30-day retention. What is the finding?

options.a: None, because the arrangement is organisation-wide and covers the models that are in use
options.b: A failed check, because the arrangement excludes anything that must keep content for thirty days
options.c: A minor warning, since thirty days is short enough to be treated as nothing kept
options.d: None, provided the deployment's audit log is set to expire after thirty days

explanation.b: A model that requires 30-day retention cannot meet a zero-retention requirement.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the arrangement "excludes models that need 30-day retention" so it does not cover every model.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the requirement is zero, and the page says the model "is part of the check".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the model is part of the check and not only the platform", and the audit log does not change what the provider retains.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Wren Logistics must keep audit entries for at least 90 days and at most 365. An entry is 400 days old, and counsel has placed it under a legal hold. What does the purge rule do?

options.a: Purges it, because the ceiling applies to every entry alike
options.b: Purges the entry and keeps a copy for a further ninety days
options.c: Retains it, because that order outranks the time limits
options.d: Retains it until the next audit closes, then purges it as usual

explanation.c: A legal hold keeps an entry whatever its age.
explanation.a: Ruled out because an entry under a hold "is never removed, whatever its age".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the hold "keeps the entry itself and not a copy made at purge time", so nothing is removed first.
explanation.d: Ruled out because no audit date decides: "A hold ends only when counsel releases it".
